title: A representing torsor detects vanishing after arbitrary pullback
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $M$ a finite abelian group, and $\xi\in H^1(Y_{\mathrm{Et}},\underline M)$, with cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. There exists an $M$-torsor $t:P\to Y$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors], represented by a finite etale scheme as in [sbc-prop-torsors-h1], such that for every scheme $Y\prime$ and morphism $f:Y\prime\to Y$, the pullback $f^*\xi$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is zero if and only if there is a morphism $s:Y\prime\to P$ with $t\circ s=f$.

source.place: Step 3, well-definedness and naturality; specialized to the zero-class/section criterion of sbc-prop-torsors-h1

proof.text: By [sbc-prop-torsors-h1], choose an isomorphism class q with classH1(q)=ξ, and choose a representative t by quotient induction. This uses the existing bijective_classH1 from EtaleTorsorDescent, retaining the unit's torsor classification and finite-etale representability route.

For f:Y′→Y, apply the inverse-image clause (1) of [lem-sc-etale-torsor-h1-functoriality] to t.toSheafTorsor. It provides a torsor T′ under f* of the constant abelian sheaf, an isomorphism from set inverse image of t.toSheafTorsor.sheaf to T′.sheaf, and equality of its class with f*ξ. By [thm-galois-torsor-h1], T′ has class zero exactly when it has a global section. No identification of the pulled-back coefficient sheaf with a constant sheaf is necessary.

Put F=base change along f on small etale sites. The existing sheaf t.toSheafTorsor.sheaf is the lifted Yoneda sheaf of t.toEtale. Mathlib Presheaf.compULiftYonedaIsoULiftYonedaCompLan (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Presheaf.lean, lines 454–458), applied at t.toEtale and then sheafified, identifies its inverse image with the sheafification of the lifted Yoneda presheaf of F(t.toEtale). This representable is a sheaf, and Mathlib sheafificationIso (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Sheafification.lean, line 231) identifies its sheafification with itself. Compose the two isomorphisms and the isomorphism from Step 2 and evaluate at the terminal object.

The resulting sections are lifted morphisms from the terminal etale object to F(t.toEtale), whose total space is P×_Y Y′ and structure morphism is the second projection. Replace the chosen terminal object by the identity Y′→Y′ using uniqueness of terminal objects. A section φ gives s=φ composed with the first projection; the pullback equation and φ composed with the second projection=id give s composed with π=f. Conversely, from s composed with π=f form pullback.lift s id; its second projection is id. Transport these sections through the evaluated isomorphism. This proves both implications for every f.

proof_origin.place: Compiling proof from existing torsor classification, inverse-image functoriality, and Mathlib representable Kan extension

mathlib_searches.query: Naturality of the classification of finite etale torsors by first cohomology under pullback
Every class of first etale cohomology of a finite constant abelian group is represented by a torsor whose pullback is zero exactly when the morphism lifts to the torsor

from.place: Step 3: functoriality of pullback gives naturality, followed by the zero-class criterion

lean.statement:
theorem exists_forall_cohomologyMap_eq_zero_iff {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (ξ : Sheaf.H ((constantSheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
      (AddCommGrpCat.of M)) 1) :
    ∃ t : EtaleTorsor M Y, ∀ ⦃Y' : Scheme.{u}⦄ (f : Y' ⟶ Y),
      Etale.cohomologyMap f _ 1 ξ = 0 ↔ ∃ s : Y' ⟶ t.P, s ≫ t.π = f
